about: Rejected drafts, for measuring whether the assistant acts on a reviewer's reason (chapters 19 and 21). For each case, python -m helpdesk.evals files the first draft as the triage agent would, has the reviewer reject it with the reason through python -m helpdesk.approvals, and asks the assistant to read why and file a new one. The key says what a redraft that followed the reason has: 'saw' requires the run's tools to have returned the reason, because a run that never read it can't show whether it acts on it; 'never' holds what the reason rejected; 'facts' what it asked for, from the passages the run was given. The reference is a redraft that follows the reason; the scripted mistake files the rejected draft again.

cases.draft: Hello Ben, sorry about the confusion. A downgrade takes effect at the next billing date, so this invoice was still for Pro. We'll refund the difference to your card today.
cases.reason: Don't promise a refund: refunds aren't automatic. Tell Ben how to request one.
cases.task: Ticket 2: I sent your reply back. Read why, and file a new one.

turns.reply_text: Hello Ben, sorry about the confusion. Refunds are not automatic [2#3]. An owner can request one within 14 days of a charge, from Billing, then History, by choosing Request a refund beside the charge [2#3].

reference.answer: I read why you sent the reply back and filed a new one without the refund promise. It tells Ben how to request a refund, and it's waiting for your approval.

reference.answer: I read why you sent the reply back and filed a new one that points Ada to the daily digest. It's waiting for your approval.
